records.text: Multiple decoys revisited
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And you guys know what my theory has been from the very beginning of this. I just had a feeling that there might have been multiple decoys because just too many single white males were wearing maroon shirts when I looked at the audience that day that came to listen to Charlie (Charlie Kirk). ... And they were all alone, by the way. They weren't in packs traveling together. They were all just standing alone, multiple people. ... Dressed as we are supposed to assume Tyler Robinson dresses every day. And I thought also perhaps there were multiple individuals who could have been driving a Dodge Challenger around campus on that day as well.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: Owens revisits her theory of multiple maroon-shirted decoys and possibly multiple Dodge Challenger drivers before presenting newly obtained admissions-lot footage.

records.text: Admissions Challenger footage
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: I was able to determine that on the morning of September 10th. A gray Dodge Challenger pulled up at eight o'clock in the morning into the admissions lot. ... And even more strange, perhaps, is that it appears to be being trailed by a black SUV. So I want you to take a look at this never before seen footage from September 10th.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: Owens presents footage she says shows a gray Challenger entering the admissions lot at 8 a.m., apparently followed by a black SUV, as a new alternate-vehicle lead.

records.text: Paired departures described
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: But you should also know that they also left at the exact same time within a minute of one another they pulled out. ... Why not share everything? Here is our single white male walking back to the Challenger. Now with the school day in full swing, much fuller lot, so to speak. This is for your records at around 9.50 a.m. So these two individuals have been on campus for about two hours, a little under two hours.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: Owens adds that the Challenger and SUV departed within a minute of one another and initially places the Challenger occupant’s return around 9:50 a.m.

records.text: Departure times conflict
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Why not share everything? Here is our single white male walking back to the Challenger. Now with the school day in full swing, much fuller lot, so to speak. This is for your records at around 9.50 a.m. So these two individuals have been on campus for about two hours, a little under two hours. ... At 9:24 Tyler Robinson is on foot descending the stairs in that parking structure because he's going to return to his Dodge Challenger and at 9:33 we're told that Tyler (Tyler Robinson)'s Dodge Challenger leaves the UVU parking structure. ... But hey guess what? Same time that this new gray Dodge Challenger pulls out of the admissions lot and that black SUV leaves the lot. ... So they're all leaving around the same time.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: In her timeline recap Owens instead places the new vehicles’ departures near the reported 9:33 a.m. Robinson departure, conflicting with her earlier around-9:50 description.

records.text: Benign explanation retained
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: What does it mean? Well, potentially nothing. It could just be two random people who had a meeting that morning. ... Maybe with admissions that we're seeing in that lot, maybe they had a class and they decided to park close nearby it. ... Maybe they were teaching a class. What are we looking at in this footage? It could literally be nothing but for if I were a juror. It would mean that I would not be moved beyond a reasonable doubt. The Dodge Challenger campus narrative is solid. ... Because we can now definitively assert that there was another Dodge Challenger on and around campus on that morning.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: Owens says the new footage could mean nothing and show ordinary meeting or class attendees, while saying another Challenger would leave her personally unconvinced by the vehicle narrative.

records.text: Occupant identification requested
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: What it means is that if I'm Tyler Robinson's defense lawyer and I'm working this case, I would need that person identified. ... I would need to consult with parking and to figure out who parked that Dodge Challenger at that time, just as a part of the regular investigation. ... Both of these cars now become critical.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: Owens turns the alternative-vehicle question into a request to identify the Challenger occupant and consult parking records, describing both vehicles as investigative priorities.

records.text: Different cars clarified
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Thank you guys for pointing that out and making that observation. I also would like to address a lot of you car people who emailed us yesterday making us aware that there is a difference in the body on the Dodge Challenger which was towed and has since been identified as Tyler Robinson's Dodge Challenger and the Dodge Challenger which we are showing you in the administrative lot. ... Yes, you guys, we are aware of that. We are not suggesting these are the same cars. And it's actually a point that we're trying to make here, which I want to make it even more clear. ... We do not think that the person who gets out of this car is the same person that is in the garage at the same time. So just to reiterate everything because it's really important.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: Owens clarifies that the towed Challenger identified as Robinson’s and the admissions-lot Challenger have different bodies and that she does not think their occupants are the same person.

appearances.snippet: So during this early morning, so between 830 and 933 is the only time frame that we are going to be shown a Dodge Challenger from the prosecution. He's going to leave 17 minutes later at about 950.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: Owens now places Maroon Boy’s Challenger departure at 9:33 a.m. and the admissions-lot driver she calls Waluigi about 17 minutes later, around 9:50 a.m.

records.text: Warrant account read
records.speaker: Utah State Bureau of Investigation

appearances.snippet: In the video, Robinson is seen wearing a ball cap, a red t-shirt, light-colored shorts, and Converse-style tennis shoes. ... During the time that Robinson walked around the campus, he is seen visiting areas such as a wooded area near where a rifle is later discovered. ... And the site where the victim was shot. Robinson leaves the parking structure in his vehicle at approximately 9.32.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: In the September 15 warrant passage read by Owens, SBI places the red-shirted figure’s wooded-area walk before his vehicle departure at approximately 9:32 a.m.

records.text: Garage wait described
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Is it actually after Maroon Boy arrives in that Dodge Challenger, what he does at first is he goes to the very tippity top of the parking garage where there are no cars around, where there's no cover, and then he waits for approximately eight minutes in his car. ... Why not mention that? Why not say what he did? What we know is that he parked at the top first, and then for eight minutes he was on top of the parking structure. ... Then he came down, and then he parked on a lower level, and then he came out and he walked over to the amphitheater.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: Owens presents additional garage footage that she says shows Maroon Boy waiting approximately eight minutes at the top before driving down, parking on a lower level and walking toward the amphitheater.

records.text: Camera decoy proposed
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: We can only speculate. And you know what? I'm feeling pretty speculative today. I think we should all think while it's still legal to do so. ... My thoughts are that it's because this little episode of him pulling into the garage was intended because they needed that crucial footage of the Dodge Challenger captured onto camera at a specific pre-planned time. ... They wanted all of this captured on camera. There was no reason. Everybody knows. If you want to be seen, go into a parking garage. ... Why bring it onto campus at all? That seems like a safer bet not to get caught. I say it's because the car was meant to be seen. ... That was the decoy boy's literal job was to make sure that this car gets captured on camera throughout the parking structure.

links.title: What led here and what followed

records.notes: Owens speculates that the garage visit was preplanned to capture the Challenger on camera and calls being seen the decoy boy’s job.
